column1: # How expensive the `creal` prelude is to TYPE-CHECK, as a load-invariant ratio.
# subject<TAB>reference<TAB>budget_ratio
# ## What this file replaces
# Nothing. That is the point. Until 2026-08-28 the only thing watching
# `creal_prelude_builds` was a "94-123 s band" that appears in four lane status
# files, is derived from nothing, and was established by lanes observing each
# other DURING a window in which the prelude was already ~8x its documented
# cost. Every lane that measured 95-120 s reported "in band, no regression", and
# the aggregate was wrong.
# See docs/research/11-design-review/2026-08-28-the-band-is-the-regression.md.
# ## Why a ratio and not seconds
# Seconds are not a gate on this box. Measured 2026-08-28 on s4, same binary,
# same commit, with one busy core competing against the test pinned beside it:
#   condition                rat_prelude_builds   creal_prelude_builds   ratio
#   one competing core               10.44 s             210.57 s        20.17
# Absolute time moved 2.02x. The RATIO moved 0.2%. Both tests are single-thread
# kernel type-checking in the same binary, so contention scales them together
# and divides out. A seconds budget on a 16-core box shared by a dozen lanes
# would spend its life crying wolf, which is worse than no gate; this one does
# not have to be loose to be quiet.
# The same ratio separates the regression at full strength. At `77b71bf10`
# 7.8x, while the reference itself moved 4.85 -> 5.22 s (+7.6%, ordinary
# growth of the rat prelude).
# ## What the number means
# `creal_prelude_builds` costs at most `budget_ratio` times what
# `rat_prelude_builds` costs, on the same binary, in the same run.
# The pin is the measured value rounded UP to the next whole unit and no more:
# 20.21 -> 21. That is ~4% headroom, which the contention experiment above says
# is roughly 20x the observed load sensitivity. Do not widen it to "be safe" --
# a budget nobody had to justify is exactly the band this file exists to
# replace. RAISE it deliberately, in a commit that says what grew and why.
# ## How to re-measure
#   scripts/check-creal-prelude-build-ratio.sh --measure
# `--check` (the gate) re-demonstrates on EVERY run that it can go red: it
# re-runs its own verdict against a halved budget and fails if that does not
# come back RED, and against a transcript reporting zero tests and fails if
# that is not rejected. A green result has therefore shown it is not vacuous.
# Measured 2026-08-28 on s4, debug profile, rustc via the repo's default
# toolchain, at HEAD of `worktree-agent-a8ff7080544ddcafa`.
